quizzes.title: Checkpoint 1 — Cloud Foundations
quizzes.intro: Cloud benefits, infrastructure, shared responsibility, IAM, and S3.

options.text: Buying all capacity years ahead always
On-demand resources with elasticity and usage-based pricing
Security becoming entirely someone else’s problem
No network access needed

questions.explanation: Cloud provides on-demand, scalable access and pay-for-what-you-use economics.

wrongExplanations.a: Avoiding large upfront buys is a benefit. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Customers still own security in the cloud. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Cloud services are network-accessed. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: An email newsletter segment
Isolated capacity (data centers) inside a Region used for resilience
An S3 storage class name for images only
A billing currency code

questions.explanation: AZs let you design for failure within a Region.

wrongExplanations.a: Unrelated marketing concept. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Storage classes are not AZs. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Currency codes are billing, not infrastructure. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: Under shared responsibility, customers typically manage:

options.text: AWS data-center cameras
Data, identities, access policies, and many service configurations
Manufacturing of AWS servers
Global backbone ownership

questions.explanation: AWS secures the cloud; customers secure what they put in and configure.

wrongExplanations.a: Physical facilities are AWS’s responsibility. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Hardware manufacturing is AWS’s. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Global infrastructure is AWS’s. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: Daily root-user work
Least privilege, MFA, and roles for applications
Posting access keys in public chat
Disabling MFA for convenience

questions.explanation: Narrow permissions, MFA, and temporary credentials reduce risk.

wrongExplanations.a: Root should be rare and locked down. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Public key sharing causes breaches. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: MFA strengthens accounts. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: Amazon S3 is best described as:

options.text: A managed relational SQL engine
Object storage for objects in buckets
A physical hardware keyboard
A subnet type inside VPC

questions.explanation: S3 stores objects addressed by keys inside buckets.

wrongExplanations.a: Relational SQL is closer to RDS. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: S3 is a cloud service. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Subnets are networking constructs. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: Lambda is often a strong fit when:

options.text: You need a fully managed custom OS with long-lived specialized daemons and no events
You run event/request-driven code and want less server management
You want to avoid IAM entirely
You must use a local optical drive

questions.explanation: Lambda shines for event-driven workloads with minimal server ops.

wrongExplanations.a: Heavy OS control often fits EC2 better. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Lambda still requires permissions. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Optical drives are irrelevant. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: EBS differs from S3 mainly because EBS is:

options.text: A global CDN
Block storage typically attached to EC2
A document-oriented query language
An email delivery product

questions.explanation: EBS volumes act like disks for instances; S3 is object storage via API.

wrongExplanations.a: CloudFront is the CDN. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Document DBs are a different category. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Email is another service family. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: Publicly open to the world on all ports
Private placement with access only from application security groups
Passwords hard-coded in mobile apps
Never taking backups

questions.explanation: Private networks plus tight security groups limit exposure.

wrongExplanations.a: Wide-open DBs are a classic breach pattern. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Embedded passwords are unsafe. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Backups support recovery. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: Virtual firewalls for allowed traffic to resources
S3 lifecycle policies
Cost Explorer charts
Route 53 domain invoices

questions.explanation: Security groups control permitted inbound/outbound traffic for resources.

wrongExplanations.b: Lifecycle rules manage object transitions. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Cost Explorer is financial analysis. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: DNS billing is unrelated. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: CloudTrail is especially useful to answer:

options.text: Only CPU percentage on one instance
Who made which API changes in the account
Which CSS class is used on a button
How to draw a VPC logo

questions.explanation: CloudTrail records API activity for audit and investigation.

wrongExplanations.a: CPU metrics are CloudWatch territory. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Frontend CSS is not CloudTrail. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Diagrams are documentation, not CloudTrail. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

quizzes.title: Final Quiz — Architecture Judgment
quizzes.intro: Apply service selection, security, cost, and reliability thinking.

questions.prompt: A static course marketing site with global visitors should often use:

options.text: A single oversized EC2 in one AZ with no CDN
S3 for objects plus CloudFront for delivery
Publicly open RDS as the web server
Root access keys in the browser

questions.explanation: Static assets fit object storage and edge caching well.

wrongExplanations.a: Single-AZ EC2 without CDN is fragile and often wasteful.
wrongExplanations.c: RDS is a database, not a static web server.
wrongExplanations.d: Browser-exposed root keys are catastrophic. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: Least privilege for a thumbnail Lambda reading bucket A and writing bucket B means:

options.text: AdministratorAccess on the account
Only the specific s3 read/write actions on those bucket resources
s3:* on every bucket in every account
Disabling CloudTrail to hide actions

questions.explanation: Grant only required actions on required resources. That distinction is central to applying the lesson correctly.

wrongExplanations.a: Admin rights are excessive. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Wildcard everything violates least privilege. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Disabling audit logging increases risk. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: Multiple Availability Zones primarily help with:

options.text: Cheaper coffee in the office
Higher availability when one zone has issues
Deleting IAM permanently
Avoiding all monitoring

questions.explanation: Spreading capacity across AZs improves resilience to zone failure.

wrongExplanations.a: Unrelated perk. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: IAM remains essential. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Monitoring remains essential. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

questions.prompt: A sudden AWS bill spike should first lead you to:

options.text: Ignore it until next year
Inspect Cost Explorer/budgets, find expensive resources, and shut down waste
Create more untagged idle EC2 for fun
Disable MFA

questions.explanation: Cost visibility and cleanup are core cloud hygiene.

wrongExplanations.a: Ignoring spend causes worse surprises. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: More idle resources worsen the problem. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: MFA is unrelated to cost diagnosis. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.

options.text: Memorizing logos without tradeoffs
Matching requirements to services while considering security, reliability, cost, and operations
Using public databases for convenience
Skipping budgets because cloud is cheap by magic

questions.explanation: Judgment means tradeoffs across architecture pillars, not trivia alone.

wrongExplanations.a: Logos without tradeoffs are shallow prep. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.c: Public DBs for convenience is unsafe. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
wrongExplanations.d: Budgets and FinOps habits matter. Choose the option that matches the lesson’s core idea instead.
